`Refunder.refund` in `src/refunds.ts` exists to carry out refunds under three requirements. I got this from the repo's OSTF trace data (`ostf context src/refunds.ts#Refunder.refund`). I didn't open the source file, so I haven't checked the code against these requirements.

**Why it exists** (the requirements it implements):
- **R-REFUND-LIMIT** (accepted, **risk-relevant**) says a refund can't exceed what is left of the original charge. Refunds above 500.00 in one UTC day for an account also need a second approval. It controls the risk RISK-REFUND-ABUSE, where a compromised account or a mistaken operator drains funds through refunds. It refines the need N-REFUNDS: customers get refunds quickly without the business losing money to abuse.
- **R-REFUND-ORIGINAL** (accepted) says a refund goes back to the payment method of the charge it refunds, never to another one. The link is tagged in the code with `@req`. `Gateway` and `Processor.receipt` in `src/payments.ts` implement the same requirement.
- **R-AUDIT-MONEY** (accepted) says every charge and refund appends an audit entry with the time, account, action, amount and receipt. It refines the need N-ACCOUNT-SAFE. `Processor.charge` implements it for charges.

All three links from `refund` are currently valid.

**Tests that cover it:** these are the tests linked to those requirements. None is linked to `refund` directly.
- `src/refunds.test.ts#Refunder > refunds to the original transaction` verifies R-REFUND-ORIGINAL and R-AUDIT-MONEY.
- `src/refunds.test.ts#Refunder > totals refunds per account and UTC day` verifies R-REFUND-LIMIT.
- `src/refunds.test.ts#checkRefundLimit` verifies R-REFUND-LIMIT. It tests the helper `checkRefundLimit`, which also implements that requirement.
- `src/payments.test.ts#Processor > appends an audit entry` verifies R-AUDIT-MONEY. It tests the charge side.

R-REFUND-LIMIT is risk-relevant, so I'd ask you before changing `refund`. I didn't run the tests or change any files.
